instruction: Generate a new layer in the image with the name 'Circle'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new layer named 'Circle' in GIMP. The evaluator checks the GIMP config file (gimprc) to verify that the 'layer-new-name' setting is set to 'Circle'. Uses the existing check_config_status metric function which parses the gimprc file and checks for the expected key-value pair. No custom functions needed as this reuses the original task's evaluation pattern with a different layer name.
metadata.verification: The evaluator reuses the existing check_config_status function to verify the layer-new-name config value matches 'Circle'. This is verified by understanding that GIMP stores the last-used layer name in the gimprc configuration file.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic is semantically correct - it verifies that GIMP's config file (gimprc) contains the layer-new-name setting with value 'Circle', which indicates the user created a layer with that name
The check_config_status metric at gimp.py:517-539 correctly parses the gimprc file format (key value) and compares the expected value
The postconfig properly closes GIMP (Ctrl+Q) before reading the config file, ensuring the config is saved
The expected value format '"Circle"' (with escaped quotes) matches how GIMP stores string values in gimprc
Minor cosmetic issue: 'type:' (line 56) has an extra colon but doesn't affect runtime since check_config_status doesn't check the type field

Semantic limitation: The evaluator verifies the config setting (proof user attempted to create a layer named 'Circle') but doesn't verify the layer actually exists in the image file. However, this is a reasonable proxy for verification since GIMP only saves layer-new-name when the user goes through the New Layer dialog
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix typo on line 56: change 'type:' to 'type' for consistency
